Moved here in from east coast. 
Since you're moving here, there's a few things to expect: 
1.	It's quieter here. It doesn't have the "big city" vibes that you can expect from places like Van or Toronto. 
2.	Nightlife is minimal at best. There's usually some events during weekends downtown, but otherwise there's not much going on. 
3.	There's SOME food variety, but not as much as you'd find in Van. Don't skip it though, a lot of places here are pretty good. 
4.	On the topic of food, it's generally more expensive here due to getting it across from the mainland, so I hope you know how to cook lol. 
5.	Public transport is okay. I don't really have any problems with it and they're usually on time. You can get to pretty much anywhere here with a bus, and even further out of the city. 
6.	People are a bit more reclusive here, so making friends will be hard, but the ones you do make are great people. I'd wager most of your friends you make here are going to be people who aren't from Victoria, as it seems to be the case for most people who have moved here from outside the city. 
7.	Lots of older folks here, so you'll be interacting with them the most. 
Things I love about Victoria: 
1.	It's super relaxed here and everyone is pretty easygoing. 
2.	Lots of local events and businesses here to explore. 
3.	Weather is the best in Canada. 
4.	Beautiful landscapes across the city and island itself. 
5.	Lots of hole in the wall shops and cafes. You'll find a favorite and go to it often. 
6.	It's just nice here if you like a more quieter lifestyle. 
7.	Lots of groups you can join from DnD to Sports, so you'll have options to meet people and have fun. 
All in all, I personally have no reason to leave, nor do I want to. It fits all my needs and I love it here. I wouldn't worry too much about moving here if you don't mind the quiet.

Moved here in from east coast.
Since you're moving here, there's a few things to expect:
1. It's quieter here. It doesn't have the "big city" vibes that you can expect from places like Van or Toronto.
2. Nightlife is minimal at best. There's usually some events during weekends downtown, but otherwise there's not much going on.
3. There's SOME food variety, but not as much as you'd find in Van. Don't skip it though, a lot of places here are pretty good.
4. On the topic of food, it's generally more expensive here due to getting it across from the mainland, so I hope you know how to cook lol.
5. Public transport is okay. I don't really have any problems with it and they're usually on time. You can get to pretty much anywhere here with a bus, and even further out of the city.
6. People are a bit more reclusive here, so making friends will be hard, but the ones you do make are great people. I'd wager most of your friends you make here are going to be people who aren't from Victoria, as it seems to be the case for most people who have moved here from outside the city.
7. Lots of older folks here, so you'll be interacting with them the most.
Things I love about Victoria:
1. It's super relaxed here and everyone is pretty easygoing.
2. Lots of local events and businesses here to explore.
3. Weather is the best in Canada.
4. Beautiful landscapes across the city and island itself.
5. Lots of hole in the wall shops and cafes. You'll find a favorite and go to it often.
6. It's just nice here if you like a more quieter lifestyle.
7. Lots of groups you can join from DnD to Sports, so you'll have options to meet people and have fun.
All in all, I personally have no reason to leave, nor do I want to. It fits all my needs and I love it here. I wouldn't worry too much about moving here if you don't mind the quiet.
